candidates.statement: [\[prop:metric inner product correspondence\]](#prop:metric inner product correspondence){reference-type="ref" reference="prop:metric inner product correspondence"} says that if $\mathfrak{h}\subseteq \mathfrak{g}$ admits a complement $\mathfrak{m}$, then we may obtain a $G$-invariant metric $g$ on $M$ by an $\mathop{\mathrm{Ad}}_H$-invariant inner product on $\mathfrak{m}$. Moreover, we may identify $T_xM$ with $\mathfrak{m}$, implying that the metric $g$ on $M$ is essentially determined by $g_x$ at a single arbitrary point $x \in M$.

candidates.statement: s [\[prop:reduced coord\]](#prop:reduced coord){reference-type="ref" reference="prop:reduced coord"} and [\[prop:tangent3\]](#prop:tangent3){reference-type="ref" reference="prop:tangent3"} give an alternative way to obtain the metric $g$ in Proposition [\[prop:metric\]](#prop:metric){reference-type="ref" reference="prop:metric"}. Let $g_i$ be the standard metric on $\mathop{\mathrm{Gr}}(n_i-n_{i-1},n)$, $i=1,\dots,d$. Then it is straightforward to verify that $g$ is the pull-back of $\sum_{i=1}^d g_i$ via the embedding [\[eq:j2\]](#eq:j2){reference-type="eqref" reference="eq:j2"} in Propositio
